question: Why does a kitchen keep the most-used ingredients on a counter next to the stove?
options: Because the storeroom is too small for them
Because most orders use the same few items, so a nearby copy saves many trips to the storeroom
Because food on the counter never goes stale
Because cooks are not allowed in the storeroom
explanation: This is caching: a small, fast copy of the data that most requests need. It works because reads repeat. It also needs rules for freshness, because the copy can go stale.
